headline: Vermont to open $31.7M disaster-aid program for farms and timber businesses
dek: Applications will open Oct. 26 for recovery payments tied to qualifying weather losses from 2023 and 2024, with first-phase awards covering up to 95% of eligible losses and capped at $75,000.
body: Vermont will begin accepting applications Oct. 26 for a $31.7 million disaster-recovery program aimed at farms, forest landowners and logging contractors that suffered qualifying weather-related losses in 2023 or 2024. The state says the first phase will cover up to 95% of an applicant’s eligible losses, with a maximum payment of $75,000.

[Gov. Phil Scott’s office](https://governor.vermont.gov/press-release/governor-phil-scott-announces-317-million-vermont-agriculture-timber-disaster) announced the program Sept. 30 with the Vermont Agency of Agriculture, Food & Markets and the Department of Forests, Parks and Recreation. The program is built from federal block-grant funding authorized under the American Relief Act of 2025. Vermont’s [Legislative Joint Fiscal Office](https://www.ljfo.vermont.gov/grants-reports/) separately lists a $31,771,557 USDA Farm Service Agency grant for compensation tied to crop, timber and livestock losses, including on-farm infrastructure and weather damage.

The aid is designed for businesses that are still operating and can document both the loss and its connection to an eligible weather event. The state says applicants may seek reimbursement for damage that has already been repaired, rebuilt or replanted, or may commit to completing eligible restoration or replanting with the funds. The program is non-competitive: applicants who demonstrate eligible, otherwise-unmet losses are intended to receive a payment, subject to the program’s rules and available documentation.

For agricultural producers, eligible categories may include damage to on-farm infrastructure, bare-ground practices needed after a weather event, future economic loss and market loss. For the forest economy, the program can cover standing-timber and harvested-timber losses, licensed-forester assessment costs, updates to forest stewardship plans and certain recovery costs for loggers reopening damaged harvest sites. Those categories reflect the different ways floods, hard freezes, excessive moisture and other severe weather can disrupt a farm or a logging operation beyond the cost of one immediate repair.

The program follows years of recovery pressure from Vermont’s storms and floods. Independent reporting by [VTDigger](https://vtdigger.org/2026/06/10/feds-approve-31-7-million-in-disaster-aid-for-flood-hit-vermont-farmers/) described the federal award as specialized relief for farmers with limited access to other federal disaster programs, including people facing infrastructure and market losses from the 2023 and 2024 events. The state’s current notice expands the practical reach to timber landowners and contracted loggers as well as agricultural producers.

Applicants should begin assembling ownership, lease or timber-sale records; parcel information; tax or business identification; descriptions of the damage; dated photographs; receipts, invoices, repair records or estimates; and records of other payments for the same loss. Timber applicants may also need stand maps, forest-management information, timber-sale records, revenue documentation and a licensed forester assessment for some claims. The state says the online application window is expected to close Dec. 31, with payments anticipated in early 2027.

The first phase is not the entire program. Vermont says a second phase will address larger infrastructure projects valued above $75,000 and up to $750,000 through a competitive grant process. Receiving a phase-one payment will not by itself bar an applicant from phase two, but the second phase cannot pay for losses already covered by phase one or another funding source. The outstanding questions for producers are how many businesses will apply, how much documented loss the program will face and how quickly the state can turn the October filing window into payments.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Vermont opens $31.7M agriculture and timber disaster aid program
seoDescription: Vermont will open applications Oct. 26 for $31.7 million in disaster aid for farms, timber owners and logging contractors with qualifying 2023 or 2024 weather losses.
